text:
sophie: Heads-up — nightly eval for rwd-v2-int6 (KB-summarizer) shows a clear spike where multiple named-entity spans are being wiped/replaced with 'N/A' or empty strings. Failure rate 6.4% vs baseline 0.8%. Pastes of a couple failing samples below.

raj: Can you paste a minimal reproducible sample? Is this seen in fp16 or only int6?

sophie: Sample below (from nightly subset):
```text
PROMPT: Extract named entities from the article:
"ACME Corp acquired Bolt LLC (d/b/a Bolt-Services) on Jan 5, 2025. The transaction value was $42M."

EXPECTED: ["ACME Corp", "Bolt LLC", "Jan 5, 2025"]

rwd-v2-fp16: ["ACME Corp", "Bolt LLC", "Jan 5, 2025"]
rwd-v2-int6: ["N/A", "", "N/A"]
```

sophie: Another failing example uses bullet lists and parentheses, similar pattern — entity tokens become N/A or empty, sometimes whole phrase dropped.

alicia: Hmm. Any common syntactic feature? hyphens / parentheses / tokens with non-alnum?

sophie: Yes — runs through hyphenated d/b/a, parentheses, and tokens with commas. Also seems concentrated in prompts where the entity spans are shorter than 5 tokens.

matt: FYI we merged the sparse-attn kernel reorder on canary last night. Could be a KV layout / unpacking regression when paths hit quantized kernels. @raj can you bisect quant/kernel changes? :eyes:

raj: On it. First steps: rerun the nightly subset locally with the int6 runtime but with kernel-reorder toggled off. If that reproduces, we'll bisect the specific kernel PR. I'll also check tokenization edge cases (detokenizer off-by-one) — sometimes those show as blank spans.

sophie: I ran a reproducible run with the same seeds and saw the same bad outputs on my laptop with the int6 binary (no runtime reorder flags changed). So it is likely in the quant path, but good to confirm.

eval-bot: Nightly-eval report: https://ci.redwood/evals/2001234567 — spike summary, sample ids: 4532,4537,4580. Details attached in the report.

deploy-bot: deploy: rwd-runtime 1.3.4 -> canary at 03:12 UTC (sha: a1b2c3)

alicia: If bisect points to quant kernel or the int6 pipeline, we should rollback the int6 rollout for rwd-v2 and pin to fp16 for production routes. We don't want downstream ingesters showing missing entities.

sophie: Agreed — I've toggled automatic promotion off for the rwd-v2-int6 model in the console and added an internal note to block canary -> prod.

raj: Running bisect now, will post logs. Next actions: (1) reproduce with kernel-reorder off, (2) run detokenizer unit tests on failing prompts, (3) if repro is consistent, create hotfix to restore previous quant kernel or add token-span sanity check.

sophie: Thanks — please drop bisect link here. I'll coordinate a quick eval sweep for other models to ensure no broader contamination.

matt: If it's a quant kernel bug we'll want a targeted rollback; otherwise if it's tokenizer/detok we'll patch the postprocess. Keep this thread for updates. :thumbsup:
